summary: Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Karin Preisendanz, Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita. He was a lecturer at Vienna (2022–2025) and became a researcher and project leader at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2025–2026).

Vlad Bănățeanu (1900–1963) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Chernivtsi University, the University of Bucharest, EPHE, and INALCO under Meillet, Benveniste, Ernout, Vendryes, Bloch, and Finot. He held posts at Chernivtsi University (1932) and the University of Bucharest as professor.

Vladimir Aleksandrovich Chernyshev (1927–1999) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Moscow State University (~1948–1953). He taught at Moscow State Institute of International Relations (1952–1956) and served as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the RAS from 1956.

Vladimir Balabushevich (1900–1970) was an Indologist and historian who served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested in 1970 and 1990).

Vladimir Druzhinin is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Novosibirsk State Medical University (2003–2009) and Peoples' Friendship University of Russia (2013–2016), later serving as an assistant at Novosibirsk State Medical University (2009) and Novosibirsk State University (2015).

Vladimir Ivanov Georgiev (1908–1986) was a linguist who studied at Sofia University under Stefan Mladenov, the University of Vienna (Ph.D.), Berlin, Florence, and Paris. He held several posts at Sofia University, serving as Head of the Department of Linguistics (1945–1974).

Vladimir Ivanovich Kalyanov (1908–2001) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under A. P. Barannikov and Theodore Stcherbatsky. He worked at the Scientific Research Association for National and Colonial Problems, Saint Petersburg State University, and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1937–1985).

Vladimir Minorsky (1877–1966) worked in Iranian and Central Asian history. He studied at Moscow State University and the Lazarev Institute of Oriental Languages. His career included posts at INALCO (1923), SOAS University of London (Lecturer 1932, Professor 1937–1944), and Cairo University (1948–1949).

Vladimir Nikolaevich Toporov (1928–2005) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Moscow State University (~1946–1951) under Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson, and worked at the Institute of Slavic Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences from 1954, becoming staršij naučnyj sotrudnik in 1960.

Vladimir P. Ivanov is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He was a senior researcher at the St. Petersburg Institute for Informatics and Automation (1989) and a research fellow at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 2009).

Vladimir Svjatoslavovič Vorob’ëv-Desjatovskij (1927–1956) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov. He served as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1951–1956) and taught Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University (1955–1956).

Vladimir Tikhonov (born 1973) is a historian of Buddhism and religion. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University, Moscow State University, and Korea University, studying under Cho Kwang, Churhòn Chòng, and Mikhail Nikolaevich Pak. He held posts at Kyung Hee University and the University of Oslo.
Vladimír Miltner (1933–1997) was a Czech Indologist and linguist. He earned his Ph.D. at Charles University (1952–1967) and became a research scholar at the Czech Academy of Sciences in 1967.

Volker Caumanns is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and completed his doctorate at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He held posts at Munich, Lumbini International Research Institute, and the universities of Bern, Hamburg, and Leipzig.

Volker Grabowsky (born 1959) is a historian who studied at Kiel and Chiang Mai universities. He held academic posts at the University of Passau, National University of Laos, and University of Münster, before becoming chair of Thai language and culture at the University of Hamburg (2009).

Volker Zotz (born 1956) is a philosopher and scholar of Buddhism and religion who studied at the University of Vienna (~1975–1986) under Anagarika Govinda. He held academic positions at Vienna, Saarland University, Otani University, Ryukoku University, and the University of Luxembourg.

Vrajavallabha Dvivedi (1926–2012) was an Indologist and philosopher of religion. He served as head of the Yogatantra Department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and as Deputy Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990–1992).
Vriti Sharma is a researcher in computational Indology. She has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.

Vsevolod Bronislavovich Tomashevsky (1891–1927) was a linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay and Vincenz Scherzl. He taught at Baku State University (1920) before serving as Professor of Comparative Linguistics and Rector at Saint Petersburg State University.

Vsevolod Miller (1848–1913) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Indology. He studied at Moscow State University under Pavel Petrov and Fyodor Buslaev, and later served on the faculty at Moscow, as Director of the Lazarev Institute, and in the Russian Academy of Sciences.
